instagram_caption:
🚀 The $20B TikTok ad surge is draining TV—here’s the timeline.

Remember when TikTok was “just for fun”? In 2019, TikTok advertising was still barely a blip at about **$0.8B** in ad spend (our tracked estimate). Meanwhile, US TV advertising was massive—around **$78.2B**—and linear TV still carried roughly **31.2%** of primetime viewership share (a proxy that tracks the real audience gravity).

Then 2020 hit. Overnight, short-form video became the default scroll, and performance marketers followed. TikTok ad spend doubled to about **$1.6B**. US digital video ad spend climbed from roughly **$42.0B → $50.8B**, pulling more of the market toward screens where attention could be earned in seconds. TV didn’t collapse instantly—but its momentum started to wobble as the audience mix began shifting.

By 2021, TikTok’s ad engine had a clear story: reach + engagement + measurable results. TikTok Ads jumped to about **$4.2B**, while US linear TV’s primetime share proxy slipped to **28.9%**. This is the year the budget psychology changed: advertisers started treating TikTok not as a novelty channel, but as a pipeline.

The real drama shows up from 2022 onward. TikTok Ads accelerated to **$7.8B** (2022), then **$12.5B** (2023), and kept climbing—**$16.6B** in 2024—while TV advertising revenue moved the other direction: about **$79.5B → $71.6B → $67.8B → $64.9B** across 2021–2024. By 2025, TikTok reaches about **$20.8B**, while US TV ads settle around **$62.1B** and linear primetime share drops to about **21.6%**.

🔥 The takeaway: this isn’t just “new platforms winning.” It’s a systematic reallocation—digital video budgets keep expanding, and TikTok is the fastest-growing slice.

facebook_caption:
TikTok didn’t just grow—it pulled measurable advertising demand away from traditional TV.

In 2019, our timeline estimates TikTok advertising at about $0.8B, compared with roughly $78.2B in US national TV advertising revenue. At the same time, linear TV still commanded a primetime viewership share proxy of about 31.2%.

From 2020 through 2021, short-form video adoption accelerated and advertisers followed performance signals. TikTok ad spend rises to about $4.2B by 2021, while total US digital video ad spend increases from around $42.0B (2019) to about $61.7B (2021). Linear TV’s primetime share proxy declines to about 28.9%.

The divergence becomes clearer after 2022: TikTok ad spend reaches about $7.8B (2022), $12.5B (2023), and $16.6B (2024), while US TV advertising revenue slides from about $79.5B (2021) to about $64.9B (2024). The audience trend aligns with the money shift—linear primetime share falls toward 22.9% by 2024.

By 2025, TikTok advertising is estimated at about $20.8B versus about $62.1B for US national TV advertising revenue, with the linear primetime share proxy down to about 21.6%.
